ImageDescription.value:
Hohllay (“hollow rock”) in Berdorf, Luxembourg
The Hohllay, also known as Huel Lee, is an impressive rock formation in Luxembourg’s “Gutland” region, more precisely in the “Little Switzerland” area near Berdorf. The name means “hollow rock” and describes a man-made hollowed-out stone that stands out due to its striking narrow passages and caves. The history of the Hohllay dates back to Roman times. Even then, stones were quarried here for the construction of buildings, which underlines the importance of the site as a quarry. Its use continued in the Middle Ages, demonstrating the long tradition of stoneworking at this location.

ImageDescription.value:
Labyrinth “Werschrummschloeff” in Berdorf, Luxembourg
The Werschrummschloeff, also known as Werschrummschlöff or Werschrummschlüff, is a fascinating rock labyrinth in the “Little Luxembourg Switzerland” near Berdorf in Luxembourg. This natural phenomenon consists of narrow, winding crevices and caves that were formed by thousands of years of erosion and are now a popular destination for hikers and nature lovers.
The formation of Werschrummschloeff dates back to the Jurassic period around 200 million years ago, when the region was covered by a primeval sea. The special geological conditions led to the formation of the striking limestone formations that characterize the labyrinth today.
